After being cleared by medical, Keman was charged with felony, second degree recklessly endangering safety,
operating, fleeing, eluding an officer causing bodily harm, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon,
and possession within 10, THC. His cash bond was set at $5,000. Almost two years later, Keman was found
guilty of all counts except possession within 10, THC. Ultimately, his sentence was withheld,
and he was placed on a three-year probation.
As part of the conditions, he must complete 200 hours of community service,
maintain full-time employment or attendance at school,
and comply with all Department of Corrections recommended programs,
including cognitive behavioral therapy and anger management.
If he violates these conditions,
he will be required to serve four years in prison,
followed by four years of extended supervision.
